detail.readme:
Fuck OpusClip.

... because good video clips shouldn't come with ugly watermarks or platform lock-in.

 

--- SupoClip is an open-source, AI-powered video clipping tool. Give it a long video — a podcast, a talk, a stream VOD — and it finds the most viral-worthy moments, scores them, and renders them as vertical 9:16 clips with face-centered cropping, word-synced subtitles, hook titles, and optional B-roll. Inspect the code, self-host it, or use the hosted version. Self-hosting is free for noncommercial use and for individual creators, including on monetized channels. Companies, agencies, team use, and paid hosting require written permission from Shiori LLC. **See it first:** [watch real clips SupoClip generated](https://www.supoclip.com/demo) from a long-form interview, or follow the [self-hosting tutorial](https://www.supoclip.com/blog/self-host-supoclip-docker) to run it on your own machine. ## Ways to Use SupoClip | Option | Details | |---|---| | **Hosted web app** | [www.supoclip.com](https://www.supoclip.com) — no infrastructure to run | | **iOS app** | [SupoClip on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/supoclip/id6784760040) — the same hosted pipeline, from your iPhone | | **Self-host** | Docker Compose setup below, or the step-by-step [self-hosting tutorial](https://www.supoclip.com/blog/self-host-supoclip-docker) — free for noncommercial use and for individual creators on their own hardware | | **MCP server** | [`mcp/`](mcp/) — use SupoClip from Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients | | **REST API** | API keys from `/settings/api-keys` authenticate the backend directly — see the [API reference](docs/api-reference.md) | ## Why SupoClip Exists OpusClip is genuinely good at what it does — AI clip selection, accurate captions, virality scoring. But your usage is metered by plan, some exports carry platform branding, and your content and workflows live on their servers under their terms. SupoClip gives you the same core pipeline without the leash: - **Self-hostable** — run it on your own hardware, process as much as it can handle - **No watermarks** — your content stays yours - **Open source** — inspect the code, self-host as an individual creator, and share noncommercial forks under the [license](LICENSE) - **Hosted option** — when you'd rather not manage servers, the cloud version is there ## Features - **YouTube, Twitch, Kick & uploads** — paste a YouTube video, a Twitch VOD or clip, or a Kick VOD or clip, or upload your own file (live streams are not supported). Twitch and Kick download providers and the optional Apify fallbacks are set in [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md#twitch-and-kick-imports) - **AI clip selection** — an LLM (Gemini, GPT, Claude, or a local Ollama model) picks the 3–7 most clip-worthy segments from the transcript - **Virality scoring** — every clip gets hook, engagement, value, and shareability scores - **Smart vertical cropping** — face detection keeps the speaker centered in the 9:16 frame - **Word-synced subtitles** — AssemblyAI word-level timestamps, custom fonts, caption templates with animation styles - **Hook titles** — an AI-written headline burned into the top of each clip's opening seconds - **B-roll & transitions** — optional Pexels stock footage overlays and transition effects - **Built-in editor** — trim, split, and merge clips, then export with platform presets (TikTok, Reels, Shorts) - **Direct publishing** — connect your own YouTube, TikTok and Instagram accounts, then post or schedule clips from the task page - **Performance loop** — views, likes, comments and shares flow back from each platform and steer future clip selection toward what works for your audience - **Real-time progress** — live pipeline updates streamed to the browser while your video processes ## Quick Start You need Docker, an [AssemblyAI](https://www.assemblyai.com/) API key for transcription, and one LLM provider key (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local Ollama). ```bash git clone https://github.com/FujiwaraChoki/supoclip.git cd supoclip ``` Create a `.env` in the root with your keys: ```env ASSEMBLY_AI_API_KEY=your_assemblyai_api_key LLM=google-gla:gemini-3-flash-preview GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_api_key ``` Then start everything: ```bash docker-compose up -d ``` First startup takes a few minutes; watch it with `docker-compose logs -f`. Once healthy, open [http://localhost:3107](http://localhost:3107), create an account, and start clipping. The backend API lives at [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000) with interactive docs at `/docs`. The template sets `FRONTEND_PORT=3107`. Existing deployments without this setting keep port `3001`; preserve that port if your production reverse proxy uses it. See the [setup guide](docs/setup.md) for custom ports and public URLs. To run fully local with Whisper and Ollama (including the Docker networking Ollama needs), see the [self-hosting tutorial](https://www.supoclip.com/blog/self-host-supoclip-docker#local). To use a different LLM provider or configure the optional pieces (B-roll, analytics, emails, YouTube metadata), see the [configuration guide](docs/configuration.md). If something misbehaves, the [troubleshooting guide](docs/troubleshooting.md) covers the common failure modes. ## Documentation Everything beyond this page lives in [`docs/`](docs/README.md): | Guide | What it covers | |---|---| | [Setup](docs/setup.md) | Docker-first install, local development, first-run checklist | | [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) | Every environment variable, operating modes, provider options | | [App Guide](docs/app-guide.md) | Screens, workflows, admin features, hosted vs self-host | | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | How the frontend, API, worker, queue, and pipeline fit together | | [API Reference](docs/api-reference.md) | Backend endpoints, API keys, admin and billing routes | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Running locally without Docker, testing, contributing workflow | | [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Fixes for the common ways things go wrong | ## Community Join the [SupoClip Discord](https://discord.gg/Sz9ZD5REXg) to share your clips, swap editing tips, ask for help with self-hosting, or suggest a feature. ## Development & Testing The stack runs locally without Docker too — see [development](docs/development.md) for the backend (`uv` + FastAPI + ARQ worker) and frontend (Next.js + pnpm) commands. The test suite spans pytest, Vitest, and Playwright, all reachable from the repo root: ```bash make test ``` ## License Shiori LLC makes this release available under the [SupoClip Noncommercial Source License](LICENSE), version 1.1. It permits noncommercial self-hosting and forks with attribution. Individual creators may also self-host SupoClip for their own monetized use without asking. Other commercial use, including use by companies and agencies, internal business use, client work, team use, paid hosting, and commercial redistribution, requires prior written permission from Shiori LLC. Send permission requests to support@supoclip.com. Earlier releases retain the rights they were released under. ### License FAQ This summary is for convenience. The [LICENSE](LICENSE) file is what applies. **Can I monetize clips I make with SupoClip?** Yes, if you are an individual creator: one person, running your own self-hosted copy for yourself. You can post the clips to your own YouTube, TikTok, Instagram Reels, Shorts, and other channels and earn from them through platform payouts, ads, sponsorships, affiliate links, memberships, and tips. You can also take part in clipping campaigns that allow you to clip the content and pay you for clips you post on your own channels. You don't need to ask first. **Who still needs a license?** Companies, agencies, and other organizations, including for internal use. Anyone using SupoClip for someone else's channels or brand, including freelancers paid to edit or clip for clients. Teams, or several people sharing one installation, for commercial work. Anyone offering SupoClip to others as a hosted or managed service, selling it, or redistributing it commercially. Using one person's account on behalf of a company does not make it individual use. **How do I ask for permission?** Email support@supoclip.com with who you are, who would use SupoClip, and what you want to do with it. Permission is given in writing. **What about the hosted plans at supoclip.com?** The hosted web app and iOS app are separate from this license. Your subscription and the [terms of service](https://www.supoclip.com/terms) cover how you can use clips you make there. Based on SupoClip.
